standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Particular Requirements for Electric Kettles and Jugs
text: This standard deals with the safety of electric kettles, jugs and other appliances for heating water for household and similar purposes, their rated voltage being not more than 250 V. Appliances intended for normal household use and appliances that may be used by laymen in shops, in light industry and on farms are within the scope of this standard.
mandatory_status: Mandatory under Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order

standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Particular Requirements for Electric Kettles and Jugs
text: Appliances shall be clearly and indelibly marked with: a) rated voltage or rated voltage range in volts; b) symbol for nature of supply; c) rated power input in watts or rated current in amperes; d) name or trade mark or identification mark of the manufacturer; e) model or type reference; f) maximum water level mark or MIN / MAX indications for kettles; g) The Standard Mark (ISI logo) along with the Licence Number (CM/L-XXXXXXX) shall be prominently displayed on the rating plate after certification.

standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Particular Requirements for Electric Kettles and Jugs
clause_title: Protection Against Access to Live Parts
text: Appliances shall be constructed and enclosed so that there is adequate protection against accidental contact with live parts. Compliance is checked by inspection and by the test with standard test finger (IS 1401) applied in every possible position with a force not exceeding 50 N. Even when the kettle lid is open, live contacts or internal wiring shall remain inaccessible.

standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Particular Requirements for Electric Kettles and Jugs
clause_title: Power Input and Current Deviation Limits
text: If an appliance is marked with rated power input, the power input at normal operating temperature shall not deviate from the rated power input by more than +5 percent or -10 percent for appliances with rated input above 200 W (which applies to electric kettles typically rated 1000W - 2200W).

standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Particular Requirements for Electric Kettles and Jugs
text: During the heating test, temperature rises are monitored continuously until boiling and auto-cut-off. Handles, knobs, and grips held during normal use shall not exceed a temperature rise of 30 K (30°C above ambient) for metallic parts, 40 K for porcelain/vitreous materials, and 50 K for moulded rubber or plastics. Outer body surfaces of cool-touch kettles shall not exceed 60 K temperature rise.

standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Particular Requirements for Electric Kettles and Jugs
clause_title: Leakage Current and High Voltage Electric Strength Test
text: At normal operating temperature, the electric leakage current of Class I earthed kettles shall not exceed 0.75 mA. An AC test voltage of 1000 V (for basic insulation) or 2500 V (for reinforced insulation) at 50 Hz shall be applied for 1 minute between live parts and the accessible metal body without any breakdown or flashover.

standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Particular Requirements for Electric Kettles and Jugs
clause_title: Abnormal Operation - Boil-Dry and Overheating Protection
text: Electric kettles shall incorporate a thermal cut-out or thermal link providing self-resetting or manual-reset boil-dry protection. The kettle is energized without water at 1.15 times rated voltage. The thermal protection must trip safely without flame, molten metal ejection, or toxic fumes. After the boil-dry test, the insulation must withstand a dielectric strength test of 1250 V.

standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Particular Requirements for Electric Kettles and Jugs
clause_title: Spillage Test and Cordless Base Water Ingress
text: For cordless electric kettles, the base connector shall be designed so that water spilled over the kettle body or overflowing from the spout during boiling does not wet electrical connections. The appliance is subjected to a spillage test of 0.5 L of water containing 1% NaCl poured onto the lid and base. The insulation resistance after spillage shall not be less than 2 MΩ.

standard_title: Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - General Requirements
text: Accessible metal parts of Class I appliances that may become live in the event of an insulation fault shall be permanently and reliably connected to an internal earthing terminal. Earthing resistance between the earthing pin of the supply plug and accessible metal parts shall not exceed 0.1 Ω when tested with a 25 A AC current for 1 minute.
